questions.q: How does growth hacking differ from traditional marketing?
a: Marketing is built into the product itself
It relies on expensive TV and print campaigns
It focuses on hiring celebrity spokespeople
It delays launch until the product is perfect
questions.why: Lesson 1 says growth hacking builds marketing mechanisms into the product.

questions.q: Why should startups launch an imperfect first version?
a: Real users and data show how to improve the next version
Investors prefer products that look unfinished
It is the only way to get press coverage
Competitors will underestimate a weak launch
questions.why: Lesson 1 says shipping fast and measuring data is how version two gets better.

questions.q: Who should you target first with a new product?
a: A small group of people who are a perfect fit
Everyone who might possibly use it
The largest companies in your industry
Influencers with millions of followers
questions.why: Lesson 2 says targeting everyone leads to bad sales and useless feedback.

questions.q: How did Dropbox use Digg to grow?
a: It hid insider jokes in a demo video for that community
It paid Digg for a banner advertisement
It offered Digg users free storage for a year
It launched a contest with a cash prize
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the Easter eggs drove 10,000 Diggs and a huge jump in sign-ups.

questions.q: What are Ryan Holiday's two tips for going viral?
a: Make sharing easy and explicitly ask people to share
Offer discounts and advertise widely
Build a press list and send samples
Partner with celebrities and run giveaways
questions.why: Lesson 3 says give people an incentive, then tell them what to do to get it.
